title: Opening Remarks: 2026 Inflation Drivers and Dynamics Conference
summary: Mostly a welcome to the joint Cleveland Fed-ECB inflation conference, but Hammack embeds a short, pointed outlook paragraph. Output is growing at a solid pace and the labor market is 'close to my definition of maximum employment', so the employment side offers no reason for restraint, while inflation has run above 2% 'for more than 5 years' with risks 'tilted to the upside'. The new element vs her Aug-10 interview is an explicit case against the look-through doctrine: the conventional view that policy can ignore supply shocks breaks down when shocks 'arrive one after another in a period when inflation has been elevated for years', because an 'inflationary mindset could take hold' and the cost of disinflation rises the longer high inflation persists. She lists tariffs and oil (supply) together with the AI capex boom (demand) as that sequence, which turns the supply shocks from a reason to wait into a reason to act. She gives no rate path and no read of the current stance in this venue, so the score is capped below her Aug-10 'some number of movements' call; the rest of the remarks cover underlying-trend measures (median/trimmed mean with skewness) and expectations anchoring beyond the mean (dispersion, uncertainty, firms' expectations).

key_quotes.quote: Current conditions in the United States indicate that output is growing at a solid pace and the labor market remains close to my definition of maximum employment, but inflation remains elevated and it has now run above the FOMC's 2% inflation objective for more than 5 years.
key_quotes.context: Her one-sentence dual-mandate read: employment satisfied, price stability not.

key_quotes.quote: The inflation outlook continues to be highly uncertain with risks tilted to the upside.
key_quotes.context: Balance of risks on inflation explicitly skewed up.

key_quotes.quote: But when the environment is more prone to shocks or the shocks arrive one after another in a period when inflation has been elevated for years, there's a greater risk that an inflationary mindset could take hold.
key_quotes.context: The argument against looking through the tariff and oil shocks; the new element vs her August interview.

key_quotes.quote: The longer that high inflation persists, the more challenging and costly it can be to bring it back down.
key_quotes.context: The cost-of-delay argument that follows from the mindset risk.
